title: Consumer and rights branches independently reserve migration V016
severity_rationale: Combining the two required active lanes without resolving their migration reservation causes the packaged migration loader to reject the duplicate version before schema planning.
environments: Proposed integrated checkout; no shared environment execution
preconditions: Both branch migration files are included in the same packaged migration directory.
expected: A unique contiguous migration sequence supports both consumer and rights schema changes.
observed: Both filenames begin V016; load_migrations stores versions by integer and raises MigrationError on duplicates at line99. Branch tests separately reserve incompatible names for16.
impact: A naive combined integration cannot initialize or validate the schema. Renaming an already-applied migration would introduce checksum/ledger drift.
reproduction_validation: Read both immutable branch files and main loader/test. No repository execution or actual merge performed.
recommended_fix: Before integration, inspect any authorized deployed ledger, allocate V016/V017 by agreed merge order, and update registry, runtime schema checks, fixtures/docs and upgrades. If a migration has already been applied, preserve its checksum/version and design a forward migration.
dependencies: Environment migration ledger observation if any database has applied either branch
effort_range: 0.5–2 engineer days if neither branch migration has reached shared data; larger if an applied ledger must be reconciled.
acceptance_test: Packaged migrations have one reserved file per version; empty and V015 upgrade paths include both features; checksum/rerun/rollback compatibility checks pass; no shared migration is run as part of this audit.

title: Rights commands remain blocked at public routing and strict startup
severity_rationale: The useful draft implementation cannot complete recipient binding through the normal mounted gateway or start in strict mode, even with service credentials.
security_severity: Not a vulnerability; existing fail-closed behavior is intentional
confidence: High static evidence; no runtime verification
environments: PR70 branch; local/development potential; strict modes refused
preconditions: Attempt the new /api/v1/transfers routes using the normal gateway composition, or launch rights_commands under sandbox/production without completing the audited service inventory.
expected: Reviewed transfer routes are mounted behind principal/CSRF/scope/recent-auth checks; the intended service has an audited trust-path entry and explicit deployment.
observed: createTransfersRouter is absent from index.ts; rights_commands has no shared trust-path registration and its executable calls guard('rights_commands'). Branch documentation accurately acknowledges both gaps.
impact: Adding the command service URL/token alone cannot deliver the advertised transfer journey; bypassing the guard would defeat an intentional safety boundary.
reproduction_validation: Read route composition and process entry; exact git-grep absence checks recorded, exit1. No server launched.
recommended_fix: Integrate coherent branch after migration conflict resolution; foundation owns mounting, trust-path audit, packaged/runtime/deploy binding and tests. Preserve strict refusal until audited. Complete the separately authorized wallet/journal/finality path rather than treating recipient binding as final transfer.
effort_range: 1–3 engineer days for route/mode/deployment handoff and isolated tests; excludes wallet/finality integration and provider provisioning.
owner_skill: Gateway/backend, foundation security and platform engineers
acceptance_test: Authenticated creation→recipient binding→sender status works through mounted gateway; anonymous/wrong-user/expired/replayed requests fail; strict startup succeeds only with audited configuration; no live wallet transaction is implied by these checks.

title: Canonical pipeline record contradicts published preview ancestry
severity_rationale: Review and merge decisions can be based on a claimed foundation synchronization that the published branch does not contain.
confidence: High for ancestry contradiction and captured PR/check state
environments: Repository documentation and GitHub review state
preconditions: Treat pipeline-state.md's claimed sync/check state as authoritative without rechecking published refs.
expected: Each status claim resolves to a published commit and identifies its tested revision; historical snapshots and corrections remain distinguishable.
observed: Pipeline says PR63 re-synced to97d54477 through75f0ff0; actual merge-base is77280249 and ancestry check excludes97d54477. Preview Stage17 says the claimed commits were unavailable. The dated pipeline snapshot also predates PR70 and later failing PR66 shell.
impact: A stale branch may be treated as synchronized or reviewed; green checks from an earlier head may be carried forward incorrectly.
reproduction_validation: git merge-base ed19dc151d103b108cf972e6d37971c55d5dcf60 0ff12fbdbce2a8b4ea1391a02ef3ea821ae6a420 returns 77280249df4e91d93b4d814b140bd5e38bba4735; git merge-base --is-ancestor 97d54477f7667dade1a4fd7220c0b2694cffb604 0ff12fbdbce2a8b4ea1391a02ef3ea821ae6a420 exits 1. Read both immutable status files and captured API metadata.
recommended_fix: Propose a single checkpoint correction generated from current exact refs, PR/check URLs and their tested SHAs; keep unavailable reported commits explicitly unverified; record who must decide unresolved approvals without treating comments as approvals.
effort_range: 0.25–1 engineer day for checkpoint correction and evidence validation; no implementation changes.
acceptance_test: Every claimed SHA resolves; branch ancestry agrees with claims; CI links show the exact head or explicitly documented merge snapshot; current open PRs and unresolved gates match metadata.

title: In-app credit has a tested redemption function but no checkout caller
severity_rationale: PR66 can expose points conversion yet no application purchase flow invokes the settlement seam, leaving the intended benefit incomplete.
product_importance: Medium; required before offering spendable purchase credit
confidence: High static call-site search; dynamic external consumers remain unverified
affected_capabilities: Applying credit to an in-app order
preconditions: A member converts points and then expects the commerce checkout to apply that credit.
expected: Checkout invokes credit settlement inside the appropriate order transaction, applying ownership/currency/expiry/retry checks with consistent totals.
observed: apply_credit is defined for commerce but branch-wide search returns only its definition/docs and tests; no application call site is present. CreditService conversion is mounted in the consumer service.
impact: A backend test can redeem a credit while an actual shopper cannot yet complete that benefit through checkout. Introducing a separate settlement without atomic order handling risks inconsistent totals.
reproduction_validation: Exhaustive symbol search at babb3604ae2f33018edf0ad45270887d4b01945b excluding documentation/lockfile; inspected function, conversion route composition, and callers. No execution or external checkout testing.
recommended_fix: Agree the commerce credit contract and connect application order settlement in one atomic/idempotent boundary; explicitly gate conversion availability if the business intends users to spend immediately.
effort_range: 1–3 engineer days for a narrow checkout integration and isolated contract/transaction tests; provider payment integration excluded.
acceptance_test: Synthetic member converts points then purchases with credit through the real application API; totals/retry behavior persist after refresh; wrong-user/currency, expired/used credit, deletion freeze and order failure cannot spend or strand value.
